tspan.tspan: Works only on a shared device registered by an admin. Sus
pended or unassigned cards are refused.
Asked on first use of that device, after 48 hours without usi
ng that device, or 2 weeks after the last PIN. A new card se
ts its PIN by entering it twice.
Five wrong PINs in a row lock the card for 15 minutes. A for
gotten PIN is reset by an admin.
"Steps" lists the steps planned for you as overdue / today
/ upcoming. "Work order scan" shows every step of a work
order in step order from its QR (or number).
From the work order detail, "Open step execution view". Vi
ew-only before approval and after completion.
A step cannot start while the work order is not approved, a
previous step / branch source / preceding work order is not
completed, a required lot/slip code is empty, another user h
olds the session, or this work location may not run it.
Check the received quantity (prefilled with the previous ste
p's good quantity) and start. The step becomes In progress
and is session-locked; the first start also puts the work ord
er In progress.
Time stops and the lock is released so someone else can t
ake over. The step stays In progress.
Time is added as a new work segment. Time on steps run
at the same time is split by the number of concurrent steps.
Entering the requested date in the step's outsourcing dates
moves the quantity to stock held by the subcontractor (sto
ck movement "Issued to subcontractor"). The list is in Out
source order (PU04).
The subcontractor does centerless grinding, coating and th
e like.
Entering the received date returns the held stock (stock mo
vement "Returned from subcontractor"). Start and completio
n are recorded on the work order's step screen.
Enter the inspected quantity and a measured value per item
. Pass/fail is automatic against the tolerance; items that ca
nnot be judged are set by hand. Sampling shows the requir
ed sample size. The step cannot complete until the sheet i
s saved.
Approve after viewing the previous step's inspection sheet.
Only passed records can be approved, and only by the she
et's approval group / approvers if set. No quantity is asked.
Record drawing/label check, protective caps, finished coun
t, spare stock, then packing → delivery note issued → shipp
ing permit in order. One per work order.
Enter defects one row each (type = semi-finished / scrappe
d / process branch, defect type, details, quantity). Good = r
eceived − defects, automatically. The step becomes Compl
eted and the lock is released.
Completing the first regrind step "Tool receipt (regrind)" bo
oks the received quantity as customer-owned stock (separ
ate from our own stock).
If everything is "Returned as-is (not regrindable)", the not-s
tarted later steps are cancelled automatically and the work
order completes at once.
Sends the process-branch quantity through another series o
f steps. Choosing how it ends (merge into main line / to sto
ck) is required.
The change is held until approved and applied to the steps
on final approval. Sending it back closes it unapplied.
The change is applied to the steps immediately.
If sent back, the steps are not reverted automatically. A red
notice appears; check and press "Mark as checked".
Branch steps are started and completed the same way, and
cannot start until the branch source is completed.
The branch's good quantity becomes the received quantity
of the chosen not-started main-line step.
In progress → "Abort"; completed → "Roll back" (both need
a reason). Not possible once a later step has started or sto
ck has been posted. Rolling back a completed step also de
letes its inspection records.
Repeat the above until every step (incl. branches) is done;
when the last step completes, the work order becomes Co
mpleted automatically. Regrind adds nothing to our stock a
nd removes the returned (not regrindable) quantity from cust
omer stock.
The finished quantity goes into product stock with the lot n
umber; semi-finished defects and branches ending in semi-
finished go into semi-finished stock. Reserved material is
consumed. All on one stock movement (work order complet
ed).

svg.text: Manufacturing — from running steps to finished goods in stock
